independent_checks_6590.py: matrix exponential and independent graph edge-coordinate reconstruction, m=1..8; t=.02,.3,1.2
correctness.rationale: Tree edge gradients are independent coordinates modulo constants. Direct subtraction of the combinatorial heat equation gives one S decay and a 2x2 (D,c) system with eigenvalues alpha_m,beta_m. The hub-edge gradient row has absolute sum a(t)+2m b(t); each leaf-row sum is q+b+(m-1)/m max(0,2e^-t-e^(-(m+1)t)-q). Positive Green convolution shows the leaf row is strictly smaller for t>0, and hub-row sign alignment forces the unique potential profile up to affine scaling. The two-exponential exact norm has derivative at 0 equal 2m-2; for m>=2 a unique positive maximum occurs at t*, and norm approaches family supremum 3 as m grows, unattained. Duality gives hub W1 distance. Independently built full graph Laplacians and edge gradient matrices, checked norms and strict hub control at 24 (m,t) cases.
residual_risks: The theorem is for balanced unit-weight diameter-three trees with combinatorial, not normalized, Laplacian.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS. Ollivier curvature and Münch–Wojciechowski characterize generic exponential Lipschitz bounds, not the exact non-exponential two-mode profile or rigidity on this family. Lu–Liu spectral double-star characterization gives spectrum but not edge-row absolute signs. Previously published related graph-heat families are not this tree and/or use other norms; a general all-tree exact heat norm formula remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The balance of local graph curvature and global heat smoothing produces a striking sharp amplification factor three, an attained full-time two-exponential norm and a rigid optimal potential. Both W1 and Lipschitz transport are natural Markov semigroup invariants; the strict peak and its absence for m=1 are structurally motivated, not arbitrary small numeric improvements.
